text:
alex: Heads-up — small-pod eviction spike in us-east1 started ~10:07 UTC. Preemptions up ~4x, latency on gpu-bound pods spiked. Anyone else seeing weird packing/placement failures?

ops-bot: Alert: scheduler.evictions.rate increased (us-east1) — group: eng-platform — link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-4321 :warning:

maria: yup, noticed that too. Correlated with the new mixed-instance nodepool we rolled yesterday (shape: c6i + g4dn-mixed). Looks like some nodes only expose a fractional GPU topology and scheduler is mis-evaluating fit.

sahil: I grabbed a few scheduler logs — seeing attach/detach timeouts and predicate failures that say "nodeAffinityMismatch" and "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" even when GPU is present. Could be PCIe path saturation or a device plugin reporting inconsistent allocatable.

alex: paste from one of the pods that got evicted:
```
Name:         job-worker-5-7f9b
Namespace:    ai-prod
Status:       Failed
Reason:       Evicted
Message:      The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage.
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  5s (x12 over 10m)  default-scheduler  0/80 nodes are available: 40 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 40 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector.
```

maria: ephemeral-storage looks like a red herring here (we saw bogus eviction reasons when device-plugin failed). Check kubelet and device-plugin logs on the nodes that got the allocations.

jen: I also see a pattern where pods with tiny CPU/memory requests but requiring GPU get pushed into NVLINK islands and then get evicted when a larger gang lands. Packing is brittle across mixed-instance shapes.

sahil: scheduler debug snippet:
```
I0612 10:12:34.123 config.go:202] plugin PreFilter failed: node(s) didn't match Pod's topology spread
I0612 10:12:34.124 binder.go:311] binding pod to node-xx: attach timeout
```

alex: mitigation ideas: 1) pause autoscaler for that mixed pool, 2) cordon the worst-offending nodes, 3) enable strict nodeSelector for GPU workloads to use dedicated-gpu pool until fix.

maria: agree. Also we should mark the device-plugin nodes with label `gpu.mig-safe=true` and add a scheduler predicate to prefer them. That buys time without hurting other batches.

sahil: I'll run a quick probe script to collect device-plugin + kubelet + dmesg from the top 6 nodes. Command I'll run:
```
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=mixed-gpu -o name); do kubectl logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=nvidia-device-plugin -c plugin $n > logs/$n.plugin; kubectl get node $n -o yaml > logs/$n.node; done
```

jen: also throttling the warm-pool downscale might help. We saw thrash when the autoscaler returned mixed shapes into the free pool and then preempted small pods.

alex: ok plan: sahil collects logs + we'll cordon 3 worst nodes, maria and jen will open a rollback of the nodepool autoscaler change. I'll post a short playbook in the incident ticket. ops-bot, tag the oncall.

ops-bot: @oncall-eng-platform tagged on INC-4321 — https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-4321 :white_check_mark:

maria: FYI, put a temporary admission webhook to reject pods requesting gpu on the mixed pool until we have a proper device-plugin fix.

sahil: logs collected and uploaded to the incident bucket: gs://redwood-incidents/INC-4321/logs.tar.gz. Starting cordon/drain on node-07 and node-12 now.

jen: reassigning some low-priority batch jobs to dedicated-gpu pool to reduce pressure.

alex: thanks team. After we stabilize we'll run a binpack defrag job to consolidate idle fractional GPUs and then run the device-plugin upgrade in canary.

maria: noted — adding followups: defrag job + device-plugin bump + scheduler predicate test. I'll drive the change and schedule canary for ap-southeast later this week.

sahil: one more observation — PCIe errors in dmesg on node-12 around 10:04. Might be a firmware mismatch between instance family and GPU drivers. I'll include dmesg snippet in the ticket.

alex: perfect. keeping this thread for coordination. If anyone sees more evictions drop a line here. :thumbsup:
